- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >2%), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive lag.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., day 1–3) when sentiment is neutral or bullish; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to first 3 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–2% downward correction starting from day 10–15 if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 77.00), model tends to hold high forecasts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversion stabilizes.
